chunks: When the married fornicator confesses, the first one to stone him would be the Imam, then the people. So when the proof (four witnesses) is established against him, the first ones to stone him would be the witnesses, then the Imam, then the people.

key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: Stoning; the prescribed capital penalty (hadd) for a married person convicted of zina, derived from both hadith and Quranic jurisprudence
key_terms.الزَّانِي الْمُحْصَنُ: The married fornicator; muhsan refers to a free, adult, sane Muslim who has contracted a valid marriage and has consummated it — the precondition for the hadd of stoning
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam; the divinely appointed leader who alone has the authority to execute the hudud penalties in full
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: Proof by testimony; in this context, the four eyewitnesses required to establish zina under Islamic law, who are here called 'al-bayyina' (the provers)

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq, who initiates the stoning when a married adulterer confesses versus when witnesses provide proof?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) sets out a precise jurisprudential ruling distinguishing two modes of establishing the hadd penalty of stoning (rajm) for the married adulterer: self-confession versus witness testimony (bayyina). When conviction arises from the offender's own admission, the Imam — as the supreme religious and political authority — leads the execution; but when it is the four required witnesses who establish the proof, those same witnesses must cast the first stones, thereby bearing both the legal and moral responsibility for their testimony. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the Imam's central role in administering capital hudud, and the principle that those who establish a proof bear accountability for its consequences.
